en.title: The Odyssey Officially Universal's Highest-Grossing Film Ever
en.summary: Christopher Nolan's epic reimagining of Homer's classic tale has shattered box office records, solidifying its place in cinematic history. The film's unprecedented success marks a major win for Universal Pictures and a testament to Nolan's directorial vision.
en.body:
In a stunning display of box office power, **Christopher Nolan**’s **The Odyssey** has officially sailed past all previous records to become **Universal Pictures**’ highest-grossing film of all time. The epic adaptation, which reimagines Homer’s legendary journey for a modern audience, has garnered an astonishing $1.684 billion globally, with IMAX screenings still contributing to its impressive tally. This monumental achievement dethrones the previous record-holder, **Jurassic World**, and cements **The Odyssey**’s status as a cultural and commercial phenomenon.

The film's remarkable success is particularly noteworthy given Nolan's career trajectory. After a public falling out with Warner Bros. over the release strategy of his 2020 film **Tenet**, Nolan took his subsequent projects, including **Oppenheimer** and **The Odyssey**, to Universal. This move has proven exceptionally fruitful, with **The Odyssey** not only becoming Universal’s top earner but also the highest-grossing R-rated film ever, surpassing even **Deadpool & Wolverine**’s previous benchmark.

## A New Benchmark for Epic Storytelling

**The Odyssey**’s journey to the top of the box office charts is a story in itself. Within its first month of release, the film had already become the highest-grossing of **Christopher Nolan**’s illustrious career, boasting a global gross of over $1.1 billion. Its momentum continued unabated, quickly becoming 2026’s biggest box office hit and joining the coveted billion-dollar club alongside other major blockbusters like **Spider-Man**. The film’s critical acclaim and widespread audience appeal have clearly translated into extraordinary commercial success, proving that audiences are eager for grand, ambitious cinema.

> "Universal reunited with filmmaker Christopher Nolan, producer Emma Thomas and their team at Syncopy to tackle the most epic story ever told: The Odyssey."

This success underscores a significant shift in the industry, highlighting the enduring power of theatrical releases for event films. **The Odyssey**’s performance suggests a strong audience desire for cinematic experiences that are both artistically compelling and commercially viable, a balance that Nolan consistently strives to achieve.

## The Nolan Effect on Display

For fans of **Christopher Nolan**, this record-breaking achievement is a testament to his unique ability to craft films that captivate both critics and the general public. The narrative arc of **The Odyssey** itself, a tale of a hero’s long and arduous journey home, seems to mirror Nolan’s own path back to the pinnacle of filmmaking after his departure from Warner Bros. The film’s ability to resonate across demographics and its sustained performance week after week demonstrate a deep connection with audiences worldwide. It’s a powerful statement about the kind of filmmaking that audiences are actively seeking out and supporting.

## What's Next for Nolan and Universal

With **The Odyssey** still playing in some IMAX theaters, its final box office total is expected to climb even higher. This unprecedented success will undoubtedly shape future studio decisions regarding large-scale productions and director-driven projects. Fans are already anticipating what **Christopher Nolan** will embark on next, with speculation sure to intensify following this monumental win for both the director and Universal Pictures.

content_raw: In terms of The Great Bag-Fumblings Of Cinematic History, it’s really hard not to rank Warner Bros. pissing off Christopher Nolan at somewhere near the top. Nolan spent an epic 18 years as a good company man paying back the studio for taking a chance on him after the success of Memento , making them huge stacks of cash while scoring repeated critical acclaim for movies like  Interstellar  and his  Dark Knight  trilogy. But the studio, apparently unwittingly, torched all that goodwill in 2020, when it massively underestimated just how furious Nolan would be when it shoved his sci-fi action film Tenet   onto streaming in the interest of lockdown-era financial concerns. (Which suggests a pretty massive misunderstanding of Christopher Nolan, who, unlike some Ithacan kings we could name, is not a complicated man when it comes to his professional desires: the biggest, loudest movies in the world, running in the biggest, loudest theaters imaginable.) Nolan broke ties with Warner Bros. pretty much immediately, ignoring their efforts to bribe him back into the fold , and taking his last two movies, Oppenheimer   and  The Odyssey , out on the open market, where they both ended up at Universal. All of which was front-of-mind for us today as  THR  reports that Nolan’s  Odyssey  has just become the studio’s highest-grossing movie ever, handily beating out previous record holder Jurassic World  for the title. At $1.684 billion (with the rest of September in IMAX theaters still to go ), it feels only mildly spiteful to note that the movie is also comfortably kicking the crap out of Warner’s biggest movie ever, Nolan’s old Barbenheimer dance partner Barbie , meaning that that alternate universe where Nolan is still cranking out his movies for WB is probably looking pretty rosy for film executives whose professional lives are currently moving slowly through the intestines of another film studio . The Odyssey  is, meanwhile, still somehow only the second -highest grossing movie of 2026 to star both Tom Holland and Zendaya . (Also the second-highest grossing, period, but that fact is slightly less fun.) It’s currently the 14th-most successful movie at the global box office, period.
